body:
### Module(s)

mini.animate

### Neovim version

0.12.x

### Description

An interrupted scroll animation leaves the window in a leaked state: window-local `'virtualedit'` stays `all` and window-local `'scrolloff'` stays `0`, and `is_active("scroll")` stays `true` forever.

Under `'virtualedit'=all`, moving the cursor in Insert mode is no longer clamped to the end of the line, so the cursor can sit past the end of short lines. Typing there pads the line out with spaces to the cursor column. This is not meant to happen outside of scroll animation.

Expected: after any scroll, window-local `'virtualedit'` and `'scrolloff'` return to their configured values (`''` and `8` in this setup), and `is_active("scroll")` is `false`.

### Reproduction

With the latest `main` and a fresh `nvim-repro`, set up default 'mini.animate' plus a non-empty `'scrolloff'` and `'wrap'`:

```lua
vim.o.mouse = 'a'
vim.o.scrolloff = 8
vim.o.smoothscroll = true
vim.o.wrap = true

require('mini.animate').setup({})   -- default config

-- Some content to scroll through
local lines = {}
for i = 1, 800 do lines[i] = string.format('%04d short line', i) end
vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(0, 0, -1, false, lines)
vim.api.nvim_win_set_cursor(0, { 400, 3 })
```

Then, in a window whose height is smaller than the buffer:

1. Enter Insert mode (`i`). The cursor line is around the middle of the window.
2. Perform a scroll big enough to be animated, e.g. `20<C-e>`.
3. Before that animation finishes, perform a scroll too small to be animated, e.g. one more `<C-e>` (a single mouse wheel notch works too, since one notch is `'mousescroll'` lines and the default predicate animates only scrolls of more than 1 line).
4. Wait a moment for any animation to finish, then check:

   ```vim
   :lua =vim.wo.virtualedit, vim.wo.scrolloff, require('mini.animate').is_active('scroll')
   ```

Observed: `all  0  true` (leaked), even long after the animation should have finished. `'scrolloff'` is window-local so the window no longer has the intended `8`.

Expected: `''  8  false`.

I confirmed this on `main` at `e4e6100` (Neovim 0.12.5). A single trial reliably reproduces it, and 5 consecutive trials left the window leaked 5/5 times. It also reproduces with the default predicate (no custom `subscroll`), so it is not specific to a user-provided predicate.

### Notes on the cause

`H.auto_scroll()` builds the animation step via `H.make_scroll_step()`. That function returns `nil` when the `subscroll` predicate produces no steps (a scroll the user does not want animated). `H.auto_scroll()` then does a bare `return`:

```lua
local animate_step = H.make_scroll_step(prev_state, new_state, scroll_config)
if not animate_step then return end

H.start_scroll(prev_state)   -- sets window-local virtualedit=all, scrolloff=0
MiniAnimate.animate(animate_step.step_action, animate_step.step_timing)
```

`H.start_scroll()` (line ~1605) sets `vim.wo.scrolloff = 0` and `vim.wo.virtualedit = 'all'`, and only `H.stop_scroll()` (called at the end of the animation step) restores them from the saved `end_state`. So when a small, non-animated scroll interrupts an in-flight animation:

- `make_scroll_step()` returns `nil` for the interrupting scroll, and
- `auto_scroll()` returns early without calling `stop_scroll()`,

which leaves `virtualedit=all`, `scrolloff=0`, and `H.cache.scroll_is_active = true` set permanently.

A fix that I verified locally, in `H.auto_scroll()`:

```lua
local animate_step = H.make_scroll_step(prev_state, new_state, scroll_config)
if not animate_step then
  -- Do not leave a previous animation's window-local side effects behind
  if H.cache.scroll_is_active then H.stop_scroll(new_state) end
  return
end
```

With that change, the 5-trial repro above goes from 5/5 leaked to 0/5.

### Consequence worth calling out

Because window-local options are saved into sessions when `sessionoptions` includes `localoptions`, the leaked `virtualedit=all` and `scrolloff=0` get persisted into the session file and restored on every subsequent startup in that directory. So after one interrupted animation, the wrong cursor behavior keeps coming back until the session file is repaired.

comment_data.body:
Scrolling is done [with side effects](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/e4e61006afcf6b399924e64b43c1168fca7b4301/doc/mini-animate.txt#L271), i.e. the state is changed during the scroll. Interrupting the scroll is usually a bad idea.

Although I am willing to try to take a look at the problem, I'd need a truly working reproduction steps verified by a human. Because if followed *exactly* as described here, it won't work (and I won't say why to not make it obvious).

> Here's what I have in my config:
> ...
> When I'm coding and have nvim in insert mode, and then I scroll (mouse wheel) so that the cursor goes off the screen, from then on the cursor isn't restricted to the line length. I can click past the end of the line and the cursor goes there. I type i to go to insert and I can type out there, and it inserts white space.
> Maybe it's my scroll function in my config causing it? Happy to try any quick tests if you can't / don't want to reproduce the issue.

Thanks for these steps! Unfortunately, I can not reproduce with either combination of 1) plain `require('mini.animate').setup()` and using the config above; and 2) my full config or clean config.

Here are steps I've done:

- Use the following `~/.config/nvim-repro/init.lua`:

    ```lua
    vim.pack.add({ 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim' })

    local animate = require('mini.animate')
    require('mini.animate').setup({
      cursor = { enable = false },
      resize = { enable = false },
      open = { enable = false },
      close = { enable = false },
      scroll = {
        timing = animate.gen_timing.linear({ duration = 100, unit = 'total' }),
        subscroll = animate.gen_subscroll.equal({
          predicate = function(total_scroll) return total_scroll > 6 and total_scroll <= 60 end,
          max_output_steps = 10,
        }),
      },
    })
    ```

- Run `NVIM_APPIMAGE=nvim-repro nvim`, wait for the setup, `:restart`.
- Open a plain test file with a lot of lines.
- Press `M` to put cursor in the middle of the screen.
- Press `i` to start Insert mode.
- Use `<ScrollWheelDown>` several times until cursor is at the top of screen for the several past scrolls (it can not go off screen, this is how Neovim works).
- The value of `:=vim.o.virtualedit` is still `""` and cursor is restricted to text lines. Tried various combinations of scrolls (regular/irregular, quick/slow, up/down/mix) to the same result. Also tried with non-default positive `'scrolloff'`, to the same result (both `'virtualedit'` and `'scrolloff'` are preserved).

If this persists, then my honest best suggestion here is to try to not scroll during Insert mode or to scroll more regularly (without changing direction midscroll). If it persists in Normal mode or if you want to try to solve this, I'd need more detailed reproduction steps (verified by human):
- Full *minimal* clean config with which it can reproduced. I.e. only 'mini.animate' enabled with possibly other relevant options (like `'scrolloff'` if it is not default`).
- A file with which it can be reliably reproduced.
- A set of steps I can follow *exactly* to reproduce the issue.

title: mini.animate: interrupted scroll animation leaves window-local 'virtualedit'='all' and 'scrolloff'=0
